newsitem.title: CANADA: Bank of Canada sets specials at 3.25 percent.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Canada sets specials at 3.25 percent.

text.p: The Bank of Canada on Thursday conducted a round of special purchase and resale agreements in the money market at 3.25 percent, traders said.
The central bank intervened after the call loan, or overnight lending rate, was bid at the top of the Bank of Canada's 2.75-3.25 percent target range, dealers said.
They said the intervention was prompted by normal Thursday T-bill auction settlement pressures and the desire of many market players to square accounts early.

"People just want to get done. They don't want to have any excess balances this afternoon. People are just taking money where they can," said one dealer. "The Bank came in and just eased the system up a bit. It's mainly the U.S. close causing this I think."
Dealers said there was a possibility the Bank of Canada could do a second round of specials today.
The call loan rate traded at 3.25 percent after the intervention. The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 2.76 percent.
